topic: Honest minimax-width uniform confidence bands for a Hölder heterogeneous treatment-slope curve in a varying-coefficient partially linear model under fixed non-Gaussian treatment-noise separation, using the accepted contour-annihilator bank to remain valid with fixed nonzero conditional L1 treatment-code error and no outcome learner; prove primitive-condition simultaneous coverage and a matching all-band expected-width lower bound.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the accepted scalar contour-annihilator be localized into an honest uniform confidence band for a one-dimensional Hölder treatment-slope curve that tolerates fixed nonzero conditional-L1 treatment-code error, uses no outcome learner, and has minimax-optimal worst-case expected sup-width?

source_refs.claim: Constructs a doubly robust uniform band for a low-dimensional CATE curve using outcome-regression and propensity-score nuisance models, but does not cover fixed nonvanishing treatment-code error.
source_refs.author: Sokbae Lee, Ryo Okui, and Yoon-Jae Whang

source_refs.claim: Provides Gaussian anti-concentration and multiplier-bootstrap machinery for honest nonparametric confidence bands without requiring a classical extreme-value limit.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: Gives expected-length lower bounds under uniform coverage and proves nonadaptation over derivative-smoothness classes.
source_refs.author: Mark G. Low

source_refs.excerpt: The shrinking-separation phase diagram, adaptive switching, and uniform inference remain open by design.
The logarithmic penalty remains necessary in a decision class strictly larger than the literal common-map class.
Resolve the band-necessity OEQ with an explicit nondegenerate undercoverage packing.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted contour bank proves a scalar ratio identity and uniform parametric MSE, whereas Lee–Okui–Whang obtain a curve band only after outcome and propensity nuisance errors are asymptotically negligible. Localizing the contour moments creates a Hölder bias and an indexed ratio process: the first scalar proof step that fails is the fixed-contour empirical-ratio bound, which must become a uniform Bahadur expansion with denominator conditioning over location and contour selection. The fixed treatment-code error must cancel before Gaussian coupling, and the scalar two-point converse must be replaced by a same-class Hölder bump packing that converts simultaneous honesty into a lower bound for every measurable band's expected sup-width.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A localized contour estimator with a primitive-condition uniform Bahadur representation and bias-aware multiplier band having uniform simultaneous coverage at least 1−α, paired with a same-class theorem showing infimum-over-honest-bands supremum-over-laws expected sup-width of exact order (log n/n)^(β/(2β+1)).

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates why an interpretable low-dimensional treatment-effect curve requires simultaneous rather than pointwise uncertainty quantification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Treatment effects vary with observed characteristics -> a low-dimensional CATE curve is an interpretable target -> pointwise intervals do not support whole-curve statements -> construct an honest uniform band under fixed code error and without an outcome learner

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over non-Gaussian higher-order nuisance annihilation, using the accepted contour construction as its infinite-order transform analogue and localizing the resulting moment in the effect modifier.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest causal PLM method showing that treatment-noise geometry can remove nuisance terms without ordinary two-learner DML.

method_exemplars.technique: Use uniform Gaussian approximation, anti-concentration for the supremum, and Gaussian multiplier-bootstrap calibration to prove coverage of the localized studentized contour-score process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After exact contour cancellation and uniform linearization, the desired band is governed by the same supremum-of-an-empirical-process object.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the testing-to-expected-length inequality to a many-bump Hölder subexperiment and the simultaneous band event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested optimality statement ranges over every honest band, so it requires a decision-theoretic expected-width argument rather than an estimator-specific risk converse.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the weak-separation phase transition for honest Hölder slope bands when non-Gaussian spectral separation decays with sample size jointly with smoothing bandwidth and fixed treatment-code error?

source_refs.claim: Derives minimax sup-norm rates and score-bootstrap uniform bands for mildly and severely ill-posed NPIV problems under primitive conditions.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Timothy M. Christensen

source_refs.claim: Constructs honest uniform confidence sets with controlled expected diameter for broad ill-posed inverse problems using concentration and bootstrap methods.
source_refs.author: Andrii Babii

source_refs.claim: Shows that uniform-band construction in an errors-in-variables problem depends on Fourier deconvolution and explicit control of error-distribution estimation.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato and Yuya Sasaki

source_refs.excerpt: yields uniformly valid inference across these regimes, and admits a matching local minimax lower bound?
Add a finite-sample oracle inequality separating contour-estimation error and selector failure probability.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted result fixes positive cumulant separation; its zero-localization radius, boundary modulus, ratio Lipschitz constant, and selector-failure bound can all deteriorate as separation vanishes. Chen–Christensen and Babii quantify operator ill-posedness, but not for a causal varying-coefficient model with fixed code error. The missing first step is a sharp sequence-dependent replacement for the contour-bank modulus, followed by propagation through the localized Gaussian approximation and a local hard family; existing benchmarks therefore do not determine when DML, finite-order ACE, or contour bands minimize width or when no shrinking honest band exists.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array phase diagram giving matching upper and lower rates for minimax honest-band expected sup-width as an explicit function of n, β, the separation sequence, bandwidth, and code-error radius, with an attaining selector above each threshold and a nonshrinking-width or nonidentification result below it.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames honest inference as a coverage-versus-diameter problem whose difficulty is controlled by ill-posedness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Inverse identification amplifies noise -> ordinary CLT inference can fail -> honesty requires operator-sensitive regularization and diameter control -> characterize the analogous weak-separation frontier for spectral treatment-slope bands

method_exemplars.technique: Invert quantitative zero-free-disk Gaussian approximation to relate shrinking non-Gaussian separation to the radius and conditioning of usable transform contours.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The band-width phase diagram requires a rigorous conversion from weak non-Gaussianity into observable contour ill-conditioning.

method_exemplars.technique: Port operator-sieve stability bounds, minimax sup-norm lower bounds, uniform Gaussian approximation, and score-bootstrap bands across mild and severe ill-posedness regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A decaying contour modulus acts like sample-size-dependent ill-posedness and must enter both the attaining band and its converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct weak, semi-strong, and strong identification asymptotics with inference valid at regime boundaries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A shrinking contour modulus creates a drifting-identification problem whose limit law and critical values change by regime.

open_problems.open_problem: When is honest adaptation to an unknown Hölder smoothness index possible for a spectrally identified treatment-slope curve with fixed nonzero treatment-code error and no outcome learner?

source_refs.claim: Shows honest adaptation over distinct Hölder balls is impossible without a distinguishability condition and gives a necessary-and-sufficient separation condition for adaptive bands.
source_refs.author: Marc Hoffmann and Richard Nickl

source_refs.claim: Builds honest adaptive bands using anti-concentration, multiplier bootstrap, and a data-driven Lepski resolution selector.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: Derives expected-width lower bounds and adaptive bands under relaxed most-points coverage, emphasizing the obstruction created by full honest coverage over multiple Lipschitz classes.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Mark G. Low, and Zongming Ma
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Provides a uniform band for a CATE function at a selected low-dimensional smoothing scale but does not establish honest smoothness adaptation.
source_refs.author: Sokbae Lee, Ryo Okui, and Yoon-Jae Whang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hoffmann–Nickl's necessity and sufficiency theory concerns direct nonparametric experiments, while the Chernozhukov–Chetverikov–Kato selector requires scale-by-scale bias and stochastic envelopes that vanish. A fixed treatment-code error breaks that template unless contour annihilation is uniform over the full resolution grid. The first proof step that changes is the testing modulus between nested Hölder classes: it must be transported through the spectral moment experiment while the same selected contours support uniform cancellation, denominator conditioning, and bootstrap validity at every candidate resolution.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if distinguishability or self-similarity condition for honest adaptation, an explicit Lepski or multiscale spectral band attaining each oracle Hölder width under that condition, and a matching all-band impossibility theorem when it fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation centers on the exact tension between honest coverage and smoothness adaptation and resolves it through distinguishability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Smoothness is unknown -> oracle-width bands need data-driven adaptation -> honesty over nested Hölder classes makes unrestricted adaptation impossible -> identify the exact condition restoring adaptation in the contaminated causal experiment

method_exemplars.technique: Use testing-based necessity and sufficiency to link adaptive band existence to distinguishability between nested Hölder classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired resolution is itself an if-and-only-if adaptation frontier after transformation by the spectral operator.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine bootstrap-calibrated Lepski selection with Gaussian anti-concentration to retain honesty after data-driven resolution choice.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the natural construction once uniform contour cancellation and scale-by-scale bias bounds are available.

method_exemplars.technique: Use wavelet projection bands and expected-width lower bounds over Lipschitz classes with explicit accounting for the coverage criterion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the width metric and converse needed to distinguish full simultaneous honesty from relaxed most-points coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax integrated expected width of honest variable-width spectral bands when design density, conditional treatment variance, and non-Gaussian contour strength vary over the effect-modifier support?

source_refs.claim: Characterizes taut uniform bands as projections of confidence sets and optimizes bands for chosen objectives, while noting reliance of many results on normal homoskedastic regression geometry.
source_refs.author: Joachim Freyberger and Yoshiyasu Rai

source_refs.claim: Develops spatially variable bandwidth selection for varying-coefficient estimation and derives local bias, variance, and bandwidth convergence results.
source_refs.author: Wenyang Zhang and Sik-Yum Lee

source_refs.claim: Constructs simultaneous bands for varying-coefficient functions from the asymptotic maximum of normalized local-polynomial deviations.
source_refs.author: Jianqing Fan and Wenyang Zhang

source_refs.claim: Defines minimax expected average width over Lipschitz classes and derives corresponding lower bounds and constructions in direct nonparametric regression.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Mark G. Low, and Zongming Ma
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Freyberger–Rai optimize projected confidence-set geometry, Zhang–Lee optimize local bandwidth for estimation, and Cai–Low–Ma study expected average width in a direct regression experiment. None optimizes location-dependent width subject to all-point honest coverage for a causal slope whose local information is jointly governed by design density, treatment variance, contour conditioning, and a fixed code-error envelope. The first proof step that changes is the optimization reduction: finite-dimensional ellipsoidal projection or pointwise MSE tuning must become an infinite-dimensional Gaussian-plus-Hölder-bias envelope with local spectral weights in both the primal band and the testing modulus.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A variational characterization of infimum-over-uniformly-honest-bands supremum-over-laws integrated expected width, an explicit location-adaptive spectral band attaining that value or rate, and a necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict improvement over constant-width honest bands.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats band shape as an optimization object rather than fixing a conventional sup-t band.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many bands share nominal simultaneous coverage -> their shapes differ for substantive uses -> band choice should optimize an explicit width objective -> derive the causal spectral analogue under spatially varying information

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt projection characterizations of taut bands and objective-based optimization over confidence-set geometries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result likewise optimizes band shape, replacing finite-dimensional geometry with the limiting spectral score process and Hölder bias set.

method_exemplars.technique: Use location-specific bandwidth selection based on conditional local-polynomial bias and variance and prove convergence to the oracle variable bandwidth.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Local information and smoothness determine the proposed variable width, so its oracle-bandwidth expansion is the natural estimation component.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the expected-average-width minimax formulation, projection-band construction, and testing lower bounds over Lipschitz classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It uses the same integrated width objective and supplies the converse template for global optimality among honest bands.

literature_map:
Fan and Zhang (2000, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics) derive classical maximum-deviation simultaneous bands for varying-coefficient regression.
Zhang and Peng (2010, Journal of Multivariate Analysis) extend simultaneous-band inference to generalized varying-coefficient models.
Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017, Journal of Applied Econometrics; arXiv:1601.02801) give doubly robust uniform bands for a low-dimensional CATE curve, but rely on propensity/outcome nuisance modeling.
Kwon et al. (arXiv:1908.02399) give functional limit theory and multiplier-bootstrap uniform CATE inference with high-dimensional controls.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1303.7152) supply anti-concentration, Gaussian coupling, and adaptive multiplier-bootstrap bands.
Low (1997, Annals of Statistics) establishes expected-length lower bounds and the basic honest-adaptation obstruction.
Hoffmann and Nickl (2011, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1202.5145) identify a necessary-and-sufficient distinguishability condition for adaptive Hölder bands.
Cai, Low, and Ma (2014, JASA) formulate minimax expected average width and contrast full honesty with relaxed most-points coverage.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Quantitative Economics; arXiv:1606.01200) derive bias-aware honest intervals and sharp efficiency comparisons for smooth nonparametric regression.
Kato and Sasaki (2019, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:1702.03377) build multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands for deconvolution/EIV regression with validation or replicates.
Schennach (2004, Econometrica) develops Fourier identification and influence-function inference for nonlinear errors-in-variables models with repeated measurements.
Horowitz and Lee (2012, Journal of Econometrics) construct bootstrap uniform bands for sieve NPIV functions in mildly and severely ill-posed cases.
Chen and Christensen (2018, Quantitative Economics; arXiv:1508.03365) establish minimax sup-norm rates, Gaussian approximations, and score-bootstrap bands for nonlinear NPIV functionals.
Babii (2020, Econometric Theory; arXiv:1611.03015) proves honest coverage and expected-diameter control for broad ill-posed inverse problems.
Freyberger and Rai (2018, Journal of Econometrics) optimize taut band geometry, while Zhang and Lee (2000, Journal of Multivariate Analysis) optimize spatially variable bandwidths; neither treats fixed-error spectral causal slopes.
prior_proposal_map:
The current stat_spectral_hte_bands directory contains initialization/state material but no proposal core or reviewer JSON yet.
The highest-priority donor is accepted stat_sa_plm_cumulant_converse/nongaussian_spectral_annihilation: its contour factorization, finite translated-dyadic bank, fixed-error scalar estimator, and scalar hard submodel were inspected.
That bank explicitly leaves uniform inference, shrinking separation, adaptive switching, and matching local lower bounds open.
Its angle0_v1 and angle0_v2 reviewer JSONs request finite-sample oracle inequalities exposing separation, contour radius, boundary modulus, and selector failure.
Active stat_functional_did_sparse_frontier/v4 was mined for its bias-aware multiplier-band architecture, primitive variance bridge, and unresolved band-necessity packing.
Accepted stat_bdd_uniform_log_penalty/v1 was mined for its many-coordinate product construction and logarithmic supremum-loss converse.
The rejected eid_dml_orthogonality_frontier/v1 HTE-band angles were inspected as a warning that coordinatewise-small drift can be entropy-amplified at a band maximum.
No archived rejected angle was found for the accepted contour-annihilator bank itself.
